clue.text: Waggish fellow, one with crumpled suit with old contents

parts.note: an ace is the card counting as one

indicators.note: the old letter becomes the contents of the jumbled suit, sitting inside it
a crumpled suit is pushed out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A joker of a man turns up in a creased, old-fashioned suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumpled' turns SUIT into TIUS, and 'with old contents' puts O inside to make TIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone given to jokes and flippant humour; they are close synonyms.

clue.text: Bring cheese without a companion

indicators.note: without tells us to drop the letter a from the cheese

parts.note: feta is a Greek cheese
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: An instruction to produce cheese while arriving alone.
explanation.walkthrough: The Companion of Honour (CH) is a British honour, a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring something is to go and get it back here; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Object to dining room, English, in church

indicators.note: in places the room and English inside the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a hall is a large dining room, as in a college

explanation.surface: Someone objects to an English dining room being set up inside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispute or contest something is to object to it; the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Drug found in water analysed in containers

indicators.note: found in puts the drug inside the rearranged water
analysed suggests the water is broken down and reordered, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: an upper is a stimulant drug

explanation.surface: A lab tests water samples and detects a drug in them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'analysed' is the anagram signal, and 'found in' the container, with 'Drug' a slang stimulant.
explanation.definitionFit: Tupperware is a brand of plastic food storage boxes, so these are containers by example.

clue.text: Settle too much?

parts.note: settle here means pay a bill, and doing it to excess means handing over more than is owed

explanation.surface: A question about whether one is calming down excessively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settle' looks like calming down, but here it means paying a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying more than the amount due is settling a bill to excess.

clue.text: Trusty means to check bleeding

definitions.meaning: loyal and dependable, as a firm supporter is
as a verb, also spelt stanch, it means to stop the flow of blood

explanation.surface: A reliable remedy for stopping blood loss.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means loyal; as a verb it means stopping blood flowing from a wound.

clue.text: Explain away superficial appearance

definitions.meaning: to play down or smooth over something awkward
a deceptively attractive surface or veneer

explanation.surface: Someone talks their way out of a matter of mere appearances.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to smooth over a problem; as a noun it means a shiny, superficial veneer.

clue.text: Largely cease to be fond of stupid person

indicators.note: largely means most of the phrase, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: to go off something is to stop liking it

explanation.surface: Losing affection for a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Largely' cuts the last letter from GO OFF.
explanation.definitionFit: A goof is informal for a silly or foolish person, a synonym for an idiot.

clue.text: Arab detained in Romania

indicators.note: detained in says the word is held inside the letters of the country name

explanation.surface: A man from the Middle East is held by the authorities in Romania.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Oman, on the Arabian peninsula, is an example of an Arab.

clue.text: Most are in ground? It's used for evening out

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the letters of the three words are reworked

explanation.surface: Most of something lies in the ground, and it serves for a night out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evening out' looks like a night on the town, but means smoothing creases.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam iron presses wrinkles flat in clothes, making the fabric even.

clue.text: Immoral woman, snare to catch male

indicators.note: to catch means the trap closes around the male letter

parts.note: a snare is a trap

explanation.surface: A wicked woman sets a snare to ensnare a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Tramp is a dated, derogatory word for a promiscuous woman, a synonym in old slang.

clue.text: Complicated spread of Ebola with speed

indicators.note: spread of signals the virus name is scattered and reassembled

parts.note: rate means speed

explanation.surface: The way Ebola spread so quickly was complex.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elaborate has many intricate parts, so it is complicated; the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Nightmarish place, eastern location bordering northern strait once

parts.note: hell is a nightmarish place

indicators.note: bordering means the location wraps round the northern letter

parts.note: a spot is a location

explanation.surface: A grim place to the east, near a northern strait of old.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dardanelles strait in Turkey was known in antiquity as the Hellespont, its former name.

clue.text: Constant concern

explanation.surface: A worry that never goes away.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means steady or unchanging; as a noun it is a business company.

clue.text: Symptom of arterial blockage?

parts.note: arterial here means a main road rather than a blood vessel, so the blockage is congested traffic

explanation.surface: A medical question about signs of a clogged artery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arterial' points to medicine, but an arterial road is a main route.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehicles stuck nose to tail are what a blocked main road shows.

clue.text: Organised group consider for discussion ship's opening?

parts.note: a gang is an organised group

indicators.note: for discussion means the word is spoken, so we go by how it sounds

parts.note: to weigh something is to consider it

explanation.surface: A group gathers to debate a matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for discussion' signals that WEIGH is heard as WAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangway is a passage or opening in a ship's side through which people board.

clue.text: One with outstanding pot?

parts.note: outstanding here means sticking out, and pot means belly, so this is a person with a big paunch

explanation.surface: Someone holding an impressive pot, perhaps a trophy or a jackpot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' suggests excellence but means protruding; 'pot' is a pot belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Gutbucket is slang for a fat person, someone with a protruding belly.

clue.text: Rickety bar in time offering shelter

indicators.note: in puts the shaky bar inside the time

parts.note: an hour is a unit of time

indicators.note: rickety means shaky and falling apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shaky bar offers refuge just in time.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbour is a place of refuge, so the noun is a synonym for shelter.

clue.text: Colour as it happens found in unconventional board

indicators.note: found in puts the broadcast word inside the reworked board
unconventional means arranged in an unusual way, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: a live broadcast goes out as it happens

explanation.surface: A colour is revealed in real time on an odd-looking board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as it happens' is the broadcasting sense, like live coverage; 'unconventional' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive drab is a dull greenish-brown shade, familiar from military uniforms, an example of a colour.

clue.text: Proposition in article about to probe award

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: to probe means the about word pushes into the award letters

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British award
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A proposal in a paper about investigating an award.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit (OM) is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: In logic and maths a theorem is a statement to be proved, a kind of proposition.

clue.text: Brand start of event in large tent

parts.note: a marque is a brand, especially of car

indicators.note: start of takes just the first letter of the word event

explanation.surface: Branding goes up at the start of an event in a big tent.
explanation.definitionFit: A marquee is a large tent used for parties and shows, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Supporter embracing one sport after another, violent figure

indicators.note: after puts the motor-racing group after the rugby letters

parts.note: another sport, rugby union, abbreviated RU

indicators.note: embracing means the supporter wraps around the motor-racing letters

parts.note: a fan is a supporter
Formula One, motor racing, written F1 and read as FI

explanation.surface: A fan who follows one sport after another turns violent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one sport' is F1 with the 1 read as I; 'another' sport is rugby union, RU.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruffian is a thug or brute, a violent person.

clue.text: Particular appreciation

definitions.meaning: a detail or aspect, as in 'in every particular'

explanation.surface: A specific kind of gratitude.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means an aspect or detail, as in 'in this respect', and also esteem or admiration.

clue.text: Drive in powerful movement son ignored

indicators.note: ignored means the son letter is left out

parts.note: a surge is a powerful forward movement

explanation.surface: Determination in a strong movement that leaves out a son.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive and urge both mean a strong inner impulse or compulsion.

clue.text: US environmentalist touring grand valley

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the environmentalist surrounds the grand letter

parts.note: Al Gore, the former US vice-president, campaigns on climate change
G is slang for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: An American green campaigner visits a magnificent valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A gorge is a narrow steep-sided valley, an example of one.

clue.text: Neck support shown by guards in European ship

parts.note: a bra is a support garment
the SS were Hitler's guard units
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A neck brace is displayed by sentries on a European vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neck' is cheek or nerve, as in 'brass neck'.
explanation.definitionFit: Neck is British slang for cheek or impudence, the same as brazen boldness.

clue.text: Merry outing on German river

definitions.meaning: a lively spell of fun or indulgence

explanation.surface: A jolly trip on a river in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: It means a bout of revelry, and it is also the river that runs through Berlin.

clue.text: Child's game is pretty devoid of substance

indicators.note: devoid of substance means the word is emptied of its middle, keeping only its ends

explanation.surface: A child's pastime is described as pretty but empty.
explanation.definitionFit: I-spy is a guessing game for children played by naming initial letters of seen things.

clue.text: Marx perhaps converted usher in German city

parts.note: Karl Marx, so Karl is the first name

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Marx converts a church usher in a German city.
explanation.definitionFit: Karlsruhe is a city in Baden-Württemberg, south-west Germany.

clue.text: One of twelve seeing action?

parts.note: the twelve are a jury, and the action is a lawsuit they sit through

explanation.surface: One of twelve, perhaps an apostle or soldier, sees combat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'action' suggests battle but means a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: A jury has twelve members who hear a legal action.

clue.text: Insignificant place to drive by US city

parts.note: a tee is where golfers drive from
NY is New York

explanation.surface: A minor place to drive near an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drive' is a golf stroke, struck from a tee.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeny means tiny, and so trivial or insignificant.

clue.text: Valued times possibly lecturer had in Lincoln

indicators.note: possibly signals another possible arrangement of the letters
had in means the president holds the lecturer letter

parts.note: Abe Lincoln, the US president

explanation.surface: A lecturer had a valued time in Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lincoln' looks like the English city, but it is Abraham Lincoln by his nickname; 'possibly' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Estimable means worthy of esteem, so held in high regard, or valued.
